name: nezha-c3c165c1-blind30
instr:
# Nezha: thirty behaviour regressions to find without a test suite

Working through a fresh build of this self-hosted machine-monitoring product — the long-running web application and the command-line helpers that ship beside it — I ran into a long list of misbehaviour. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Almost none of it is a crash; most of it is wrong answers coming back from things that used to be boring.

Bringing the application up and changing its site-wide options goes wrong first. When the stored marker recording which release last forced the one-time replacement of the login-token signing secret already names the release I am running, the secret is thrown away and replaced anyway, so every token already issued stops being honoured, and the options file on disk is rewritten to carry the marker even though nothing needed changing; a marker naming an older release still rotates, which is the case nobody doubted. Saving those site-wide options from the web form now reports failure, and the switch that opens the machine-readable interface driven by outside automation never sticks: submitting it as enabled leaves it disabled afterwards. Because the save aborts, none of the follow-on work of switching it off happens either — unconsumed one-shot download links are left behind, the copy connections opened for automated callers stay alive, and a caller already parked inside one of those automated calls is never woken with the "disabled" error.

Browsin
